newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps flat, little direction seen.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps flat, little direction seen.

text.p: European oil swaps were broadly unchanged on Thursday with levels shifting sideways.
Brent crude CFDs slipped two cents or so, but with a very strong bid on physical Brent heard prices could rise. Dealers were uncertain whether the bid was serious or was linked in a CFD move.
June 16-20 was pegged at -68 cents under August Brent while June 23-27 was put at -57 cents from -54 cents and June 30-July 4 was hovering around -47/48 roughly steady. No CFDs were heard concluded.

Heavy fuel was also fairly unchanged with July put around $84 compared with $83.75. June swaps were effectively finished with dealers saying the contract would be used for June/July trading. Physical barges were done at $85, $85.50 and $86.00.
Naphtha swaps were holding with July valued at $178.50 and August flat or 25 cents weaker. The June/July spread was heard offered at $5.

Gasoline was very narrowly easier, dropping 50 cents on July which was pegged around $182.50 with August between $182.75 and $184.00 Physical barges went at $187 fob ARA with refinery material at $192.50.
The gas oil crack spread saw 4Q97 at $4.55, 1Q98 at $4.58 and 2Q98 around $4.05, all broadly similar levels to those seen on Wednesday.
